Carla S: Hey team — quick proposal: trim debug-level VM and worker logs from 365d -> 30d by default, keep auth/audit logs at 1y. Reason: storage costs + most root-cause data is in 30d window. Thoughts?
Ben I: Do we mean both raw logs and SIEM exported copies?
Carla S: Raw first. For SIEM exports we'd keep 90d unless a ticket flags an investigation needing longer.
Alice O: FWIW oncall often needs 90-180d for slow fraud cases. If we cut to 30d we need a straightforward escalation to retrieve older slices.
Dave P: How would that work operationally? Are we asking for ad-hoc exports from cold storage? SLA?
Carla S: My idea: implement timeboxed RBAC role `forensics-analyst` that can request a one-off unmask/unwrap for specific ranges. Grants last 48h and are logged.
Ben I: Technical constraints: our SIEM export pipeline writes to splunk-indexer S3 bucket with CMK-encrypted objects. To support 48h access we can implement a KMS-enveloped proxy that issues ephemeral data keys for approved requests.
Ben I: Pseudocode for role binding change:```yaml
roles:
  - name: forensics-analyst
    permissions: [query:scrubbed, request:unwrap]
    constraints: {duration_hours: 48, justification_required: true}
```
Alice O: +1 for duration-limited grants. Also require an incident ticket link in the justification. That reduces risk and gives auditors a trail.
Carla S: Agree. Also add a pre-check for data-minimization: if the query can be satisfied with masked/aggregated logs, deny unwrap by default.
Dave P: What about tenant isolation? Some partner tenants require their raw logs to never leave their managed S3. We need tenant-aware unwrapping.
Ben I: We can gate unwraps by tenant tag and require tenant-owner approval for those cases. For non-sensitive tenants infra can approve.
sec-bot: New ticket created: SEC-2371 — "Retention reduction + ephemeral forensics grants" <https://redwood.internal/tickets/SEC-2371> :spiral_note_pad: 
Carla S: Security question: does KMS allow audit of which principal invoked GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext? We need proof the requestor triggered the unwrap.
Ben I: Yes — CloudKMS/CMK CloudTrail events include GenerateDataKey operations and key_alias. But for our proxy model the proxy service will call KMS, so we must ensure proxy logs include requester identity and ticket id, and we forward those attributes to CloudTrail or store in an append-only audit log.
Alice O: Can we add a small retention-exempt log stream for these audits (compress+hash) so forensics checks can survive 1y retention changes?
Carla S: Good call. Keep audit-log-of-unwraps for 2y, signed, and immutable.
Dave P: Any perf implications on SIEM queries when we reduce raw retention? Also, we should update runbooks and oncall playbooks now if we're changing windows.
Ben I: Perf: fewer cold reads -> cheaper. For cases where we need older data we'll incur retrieval cost/time. We can add a low-priority async job for bulk retrievals to avoid blocking live triage.
Carla S: Action items: 1) Draft RBAC change PR for `forensics-analyst` and `unwrap-request` workflow (Ben) 2) Design KMS-proxy audit flow + sample CloudTrail mapping (Ben) 3) Update runbooks and create ticket templates with justification fields (Alice) 4) Draft compliance note about 30d default + 90d SIEM exports + 2y unwrap-audit (Carla)
Alice O: I'll attach examples to SEC-2371 and flag to SRE runbook owners.
Carla S: Cool. @sec-bot please ping me when SEC-2371 status changes to "design review".
